thread:
Carla: Heads-up — onboarding a HF z-code variant and the function-invocation markers aren't matching our protobuf-based parser. Saw things like `<invk>` / `</invk>` and also `<<call>>` in the same model files.

Sanjay: ugh. which model + tokenizer?

Carla: hf/zcode-v2-compat, tokenizer appears to be a custom BPE with preserved byte escapes. config.json lists `special_tokens: { 'INV_START': '<invk>', 'INV_END': '</invk>', 'ROLE_A': '<role:assistant>' }` but the chat templates from hf use `<<call>>` markers in system messages.

Ben: that mismatch explains the eval flakiness we saw on function-invocation bench. Our runner expects `INV_START/INV_END` sentinel pairs to emit a JSON blob — if tokenizer consumes `<`/`>` as separate tokens the boundary detection fails.

Olivia: benchmark snapshot from yesterday: invocation accuracy dropped from 98% -> 72% on our 50k prompt set after quantizing to int8. Suspect token merging changed boundaries; logs show truncated JSON in ~12% of failed cases.

Carla: posting short repro of the token stream we get (simplified):
```
input: "call tool send_email { \"to\": \"x@redwood.ai\", \"body\": \"hi\" }"
tokenized: ["call"," tool"," send","_email"," {"," \"to\""," :"," \"x@redwood.ai\""," ,"," \"body\""," :"," \"hi\""," }"]
// notice `call` and `{` separated, but our parser expects `<invk>` wrapper tokens preserved as single tokens
```

Sanjay: two approaches: 1) normalize at HF->RW conversion time — map `<<call>>` -> `<invk>` and add token alias entries in tokenizer `special_tokens_map`, or 2) keep generator tokens but change runtime detector to run a lightweight regex pre-parser that reconstructs invocation ranges before handing to eval/runner.

Ben: I prefer conversion-time fixes if possible because quantization later is lossy. Add aliases to tokenizer so `<invk>` and `<<call>>` both resolve to same special ID. Example snippet to patch `tokenizer.json` during import: 
```json
{
  "added_tokens": [
    {"text": "<invk>", "single_word": false},
    {"text": "<<call>>", "single_word": false, "alias_of": "<invk>"}
  ]
}
```
(we'll transform alias_of into same id in RW mapping)

Olivia: would aliasing change token ids post-quantize? We saw token id remapping in int8 path cause the same surface string to map to different internal ids across builds. That broke our cached KV lookups.

Carla: good point. If alias->same id is impossible across quantization, fallback is canonicalization at text layer: rewrite `<<call>>` -> `<invk>` before tokenizing. More brittle but deterministic.

deploy-bot: CI / invocation-regression-check — run started (job 7821) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Sanjay: action items: (1) Ben opens HF->RW converter PR to add token aliasing + a text-canonicalizer option, (2) Olivia runs the int8 bench with canonicalizer enabled, (3) I'll add a lightweight pre-parser in eval harness as a safety net.

Ben: I'll open PR with tests + small conversion script. tagging @Olivia for the bench. :+1:

Olivia: thanks — will kick off bench once PR is up. keeping an eye on the regression metrics and will post results.

Carla: thanks team. let's avoid changing runtime parser unless absolutely needed; prefer conversion or text canonicalization first.
